stimulus.text:
Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837:

“At every hazard, and by every sacrifice, this Union must be preserved.”

“If the sordid feelings of mere selfishness shall usurp the place which ought to be filled by public spirit, the legislation of Congress will soon be converted into a scramble for personal and sectional advantages.”

Background: Jackson spoke as he left the presidency after two terms that included the nullification crisis of 1832–1833, when South Carolina tried to void the federal tariff.
stimulus.source_note: Quotations verbatim from Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837, public domain, as printed by the University of Texas Core Texts collection.

source: original; stimulus verbatim from Andrew Jackson, Farewell Address, March 4, 1837, public domain
stem: What did Jackson say must be preserved 'at every hazard'?

options.text: The Second Bank of the United States
options.misconception: Jackson destroyed the Bank; he would not call for preserving it.

options.text: The right of states to nullify federal laws
options.misconception: Jackson fought nullification in 1833, so he would not defend it here.
The passage says nothing about government jobs or the spoils system.

rationales.A: Jackson vetoed the Bank's recharter and removed its deposits. Preserving the Bank is the opposite of his policy.
rationales.B: Jackson answered nullification with a proclamation and a Force Bill. He would not call nullification worth preserving.
rationales.C: The passage never mentions offices or appointments. The spoils system is not what Jackson says to preserve.
rationales.D: His own words give the answer. The Union must be preserved at every hazard and by every sacrifice.
rationales.general:
1. Read the sentence. Jackson names one thing to preserve at every hazard and by every sacrifice.
2. Check the words. The sentence ends with the Union, not the Bank, not nullification, not offices.
3. Name the answer. The Union is the thing Jackson says comes first.
Remember: when a writer names one thing above all, that thing is the answer.
